六级大纲词汇 · 07英文原文

The Price on the Last Page

账本最后一页的价格 · 593 词 · 7 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A repair cooperative sold used kettles and radios at nominal prices. A slump in turnover threatened its rent, and a new tariff on imported parts made costs volatile. Then a prosperous wholesale dealer offered a premium for its inventory. The offer looked lucrative. It would also leave local families with no merchandise to buy. Imani, the thrifty treasurer, asked members to defer their vote until she could appraise the stock. Why would a shrewd dealer pay more than their own appraisal?

2During fiscal turmoil, routine auditing revealed two omissions. Some spare parts had depreciated while the shop counted them at full price. After a deduction for scrap value, the cooperative would incur a loss on them. A reputable auditor checked the dealer's portfolio of rare radios. He could deduct collection costs from the price and leave the obsolete stock behind. His aggregate figure therefore overstated the real return. The audit made the committee look at depreciation as well as cash.

3Imani proposed an auction for rare radios and a fixed price for staple items. The auctioneer gave a concession and slashed his fee for a monthly slot. Local customers could subscribe to a repair service, while the shop would swap unused parts with another franchise. Each subscriber would pay in installments. If the shop defaulted on a booking, it would refund the fee. This modest subscription would bolster revenue without leaving a family indebted over a broken kettle.

4At the first auction a bidder presented counterfeit notes. Imani revised the payment rules, then made a tentative offer. The wholesaler could bid for items left after two sales. He threatened to withhold his bid. The terms reduced his leverage and price volatility. A policy to deregulate the market had opened it to competitors. He wanted to use deregulation to monopolize the supply and restore a monopoly. Two firms made legitimate bids after a tactful invitation. Their brisk competition raised enough money to offset a recent rent hike and gave the trial momentum.

5The first fiscal report showed a cumulative gain, but a levy on waste disposal still strained the shop. Imani could solicit a subsidy or seek a modest allotment of benches from the treasury. An endowment could finance training later. Another donor might endow the course. It made no sense to subsidize the same class twice. For now the benches would allow an apprentice to repair a kettle while another worked on a radio. The council would allot the benches if the cooperative published its audit and kept the course open to nonmembers.

6At the next meeting, members debated a small dividend. Imani showed how a reserve would protect them from volatile demand and how a separate allocation could exempt customers with no income from the service fee. The exemption had a fixed expiration so they could review its effect. One member favored a price cut. Imani argued for equity through a waiver, which would trim costs for those who needed it. The committee chose the reserve. Its thrift made a more equitable plan possible.

7The wholesaler returned with a smaller offer. He wanted to merge the repair service with his own and rename it. The merger promised prosperity, yet it might lure new buyers at the cost of a downgrade for local customers. The shop could prosper on its own. Imani let the offer lapse. She put his offer beside the proceeds from ordinary sales. A new volunteer asked which figure mattered more. She turned to the last page and showed him how many kettles the shop had sent home that week.

六级大纲词汇 · 07中文译文

账本最后一页的价格

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一家维修合作社以很低的价格卖二手水壶和收音机。营业额下滑，房租快交不起了。进口零件加征的关税又让成本忽高忽低。一位生意兴隆的批发商提出加价买走店里所有存货。条件很诱人，可货架一空，附近的家庭也就买不到东西了。精打细算的财务负责人伊玛妮请大家推迟表决，等她评估完库存。一个精明的商人为什么愿意出比他们估价更高的钱？

2财务动荡期间，例行审计找出了两处遗漏。有些配件已经贬值，账上却还按原价算。即便扣掉能卖废品的钱，合作社在这些配件上还是要亏损。一位有信誉的审计员查看了批发商经手的稀有收音机。批发商可以从报价里扣除取货成本，也可以把过时的存货留下。把这两笔都算进去，他报的总价就夸大了实际收益。委员会这才开始同时看现金和折旧。

3伊玛妮提议拍卖稀有收音机，日常用品则定价出售。拍卖师作了让步，大幅降低每月固定场次的费用。附近的顾客可以订购维修服务，店里则和另一家连锁店交换用不上的零件。订户分期付款。如果维修铺不能按预约履约，就退回费用。少量订阅收入就能帮店里撑下去，普通家庭也不必为一只坏水壶背债。

4第一次拍卖，有人拿假钞付款。伊玛妮修改收款规则，再给批发商提出一个暂定方案，两次拍卖后剩下的东西，他可以出价竞买。他威胁说要退出。新条件削弱了他的谈判筹码，也降低了价格波动。放宽管制本来让更多人可以入场，他却想借此垄断货源。伊玛妮委婉地邀请了另外两家商户，两家都按规则出了价。竞价很活跃，所得抵消了最近涨的房租，也让这个试验有了继续做下去的动力。

5第一份财务报告显示，累计收入有所增加，废弃物处理费仍给店里带来压力。伊玛妮可以申请补贴，也可以请市财政划给店里几张闲置的工作台。以后或许有一笔捐赠基金能资助培训，也可能有另一位捐赠人出资办课，同一门课没必要补贴两次。眼下有几张工作台，就能让两位学徒同时修水壶和收音机。市议会同意划拨，条件是合作社公布审计结果，并让非会员也能来上课。

6下次开会时，大家讨论要不要分一点红利。伊玛妮说明，储备金能帮店里应付需求波动，还可以另留一笔钱，免掉无收入顾客的服务费。减免设有截止日期，届时可以检查效果。有人更愿意普遍降价。伊玛妮认为有针对性的减免更公平，能直接减轻有需要的人的负担。委员会选择留储备金。省下来的钱，让这套办法有了实行的余地。

7批发商带着一份金额更小的报价回来。他想把维修服务并入自己的业务，再换个名字。合并看起来有发展前景，也可能招来新顾客，却降低附近居民能获得的服务。维修铺自己也能经营下去。伊玛妮让报价过期，把它和日常收入记在一起。一名新志愿者问，哪个数字更重要。她翻到最后一页，给他看铺子那一周让多少只水壶重新回到了顾客家里。
